title: Securities Dealing Policy
tiers: BHP directors, employees and contractors | Persons on insider lists | Participants in BHP's employee incentive plans | Restricted Persons | PDMRs | PCAs
ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board or the Disclosure Committee may declare any other period a Closed Period. The policy is silent on whether such a declaration is confidential.
financing_disclosure: PDMRs and PCAs; inception (entry into any margin lending or other secured financing arrangement is a dealing); Group Company Secretary; immediately after dealing, with BHP notifying the FCA within three business days and announcing to exchanges within two business days of notification
exemption_authority: Clearance Officers (Group Company Secretary or delegate) may give or refuse clearance at their discretion and may clear a PDMR, PCA or Restricted Person to deal in a Closed Period in exceptional circumstances; only the Group Company Secretary or the Chair of the Board may determine that severe financial difficulty or other exceptional circumstances exist. The Board or Disclosure Committee declares additional Closed Periods.
external_documents: Securities Dealing Clearance Request Form | BHP insider lists maintained by Group Governance | Employee incentive plan rules (Cash and Deferred Plan, Long Term Incentive Plan, Management Award Plan, Short-Term Incentive Plan)
jurisdiction_overlays: UK Market Abuse Regulation concepts: PDMRs, PCAs, insider lists, FCA notification of PDMR/PCA dealings within three business days
summary: A funded collar over vested, unrestricted shares is possible for a BHP PDMR (director or KMP) but only with prior written clearance from the Group Company Secretary, executed within two business days of clearance, outside Closed Periods (year-end and half-year-end to results, plus any Board or Disclosure Committee blackout) and with a tenor exceeding one year, since investments maturing in one year or less are prohibited short-term dealings. The express PDMR derivatives ban is limited to exchange-traded or organised-market instruments, so a bilateral OTC put and call is caught only as a dealing, though BHP applies a substance-over-form approach and clearance is discretionary. Unvested securities and vested securities under holding locks cannot be hedged or used as collateral at all, so only free vested shares can be collared or charged. The loan and the security interest over the shares are each dealings requiring clearance and, for PDMRs, post-trade notification to the Group Company Secretary with onward FCA and exchange disclosure. The policy is silent on forced sales by a lender in a Closed Period, and the exceptional-circumstances relief covers only an immediate sale.

title: Group Personal Trading Policy
tiers: all employees | Specified Persons | CBA Board directors, Group Company Secretaries, Group Executives
ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The CBA Board (or its delegate) designates Trading Windows and may vary, suspend or close them at any time; Specified Persons are notified by e-mail and on the Conflicts Hub. Confidentiality of a suspension is not addressed.
exemption_authority: Group Chief Risk Officer is the Policy Exemption Authority. Trading Window exceptions are approved under Attachment A (CBA Board Chair for directors and the CEO; Board Audit Committee Chair for the Board Chair; CEO for Group Executives; Subsidiary Board Chair or Deputy Chair for subsidiary directors; Group General Counsel and Group Executive Legal & Group Secretariat for other Specified Persons and Board company secretaries). Any other exemption request goes through the Group Policy Framework.
external_documents: Group Personal Trading Procedure (Pre-Clearance mechanics, who requires it and for which Trades, brokerage account declarations, attestations) | Conflicts Hub (Specified Person designation, Pre-Clearance requests, Trading Window notifications) | Group Policy Framework Glossary | Group Policy Framework (process for exemption requests other than Trading Window exceptions) | Group Conflicts Management Policy | Group Issue Management Procedure | Group Incident Management Procedure | ASB securities trading policy | Additional BU/SU Securities Trading requirements
jurisdiction_overlays: UK and EU Market Abuse Regulation No 596/2014: CBA Board directors, Group Company Secretaries, Group Executives and their Associates must not Trade any Group Security listed or traded on a UK or EU regulated market, or any other Security whose price or value depends on or affects such a Group Security (para 18). | Where laws, regulatory requirements or contractual obligations conflict with the policy, the more stringent standard applies. | ASB (New Zealand) has its own securities trading policy.
summary: A funded collar is not possible for CBA Board directors, Group Company Secretaries, Group Executives or their Associates: para 9 bans any transaction that limits the economic risk of their exposure to any vested Group Securities, and para 16(a) bans using Group Securities as security for margin lending or any other secured financing. For other Specified Persons (e.g. Executive General Managers, Subsidiary Board directors, Group Control Room staff), the hedge leg over vested shares free of any holding lock is not expressly banned, but the OTC options are Securities and entering them is a Trade, so it must be done in a Trading Window, with Pre-Clearance where designated on the Conflicts Hub (valid three business days), subject to the 30-day LIFO holding rule, and it must not involve CFDs, short selling or stock lending of Group Securities. The loan leg secured on the collared shares is prohibited for all Specified Persons, so at most an unsecured or unfunded collar is workable for that group, and exercise or settlement mechanics that execute outside a Trading Window are a further risk under para 11. Employees who are not Specified Persons face only the insider trading prohibition and whatever Pre-Clearance the unpublished Procedure imposes. The MAR overlay in para 18 adds an outright bar for the senior group on any Security that prices off a UK/EU-listed Group Security.

title: Dealing in Securities Policy
tiers: Origin Personnel | Directors | ELT & ELT Direct Reports | All other employees | Associates
ad_hoc_blackout_authority: Company Secretary, in conjunction with the Chief Executive Officer, may impose and lift an 'Additional Prohibition' due to activity or knowledge within Origin. Confidential: it is unlikely to be announced; a person requesting clearance may be told on a confidential basis that a prohibition exists but not why or for how long.
exemption_authority: None. Dealing during a Closed Period or Additional Prohibition 'will not be permitted' (8.2) and there is no hardship or discretionary waiver; the Board approves only material changes to the Policy.
summary: A funded collar is not possible under this policy. The unfunded derivative legs (purchased put and written call) over vested shares are a Dealing that Directors may enter with prior written clearance from the Chairman and Company Secretary (Manager and Company Secretary for ELT and their direct reports), executed within 2 business days, outside the 1 July and 1 January Closed Periods and any confidential Additional Prohibition, and not over plan securities that remain unvested or subject to performance hurdles. However, section 7.1 expressly bans margin lending and any other secured financing arrangement in respect of Origin Securities for all personnel and their Associates, with no exemption authority, so a loan secured on the collared shares is prohibited outright. A lender's forced sale in a Closed Period is a serious breach that may lead to dismissal, and there is no hardship relief. Tenor should exceed three months to avoid the short-term dealing ban, and any unwind or settlement is itself a Dealing requiring fresh clearance.
